source.title: Some Open Problems in Asymptotic Geometric Analysis

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0, independent of the dimension n, such that every centered convex body K in R^n with volume |K| = 1 has at least one hyperplane section through the origin whose (n-1)-dimensional volume is greater than c?
accepted.context_brief: hyperplane conjecture for centered convex bodies

accepted.question_text: Let K be a convex body in R^n. After applying a nondegenerate affine transformation, place K in isotropic position: |K| = 1, its center of mass is at the origin, and its inertia matrix is a scalar multiple of the identity, so there is a number L_K > 0 such that integral_K <x, theta>^2 dx = L_K^2 for every unit vector theta. Is there an absolute constant C, independent of n and K, such that L_K <= C for all dimensions and all convex bodies?

For a fixed p > 0 and an n-dimensional convex body K, choose n+1 points x_1, ..., x_{n+1} independently and uniformly in K and let m_p(K) be the normalized p-th moment of the volume of the random simplex conv{x_1, ..., x_{n+1}}. Determine, up to nondegenerate affine transformations, which convex bodies minimize m_p(K) and which convex bodies maximize m_p(K); in particular, settle the open maximization direction in dimensions n >= 3.

evidence.quote: In the opposite direction the problem is open if n >= 3.

accepted.question_text: For an n-dimensional convex body K, let m_1(K) be the expected normalized volume of the random simplex conv{x_1, ..., x_{n+1}} generated by n+1 independent uniformly distributed points in K. Is it true that m_1(K) <= m_1(S_n) for every convex body K in R^n, where S_n is any n-dimensional simplex?
accepted.context_brief: simplex conjecture for random simplex volume
